newsitem.title: USA: McLeodUSA, Consolidated Communications to merge.
newsitem.headline: McLeodUSA, Consolidated Communications to merge.

text.p: McLeodUSA Inc, a competitive local exchange carrier, and Consolidated Communications Inc, said on Monday that they have signed a definitive merger agreement.

The transaction, valued at about $420 million, was unanimously approved by the board of directors of each company. Under the agreement, owners of telecommunications company Consolidated Communications will receive 8.49 million shares of McLeodUSA stock and $155 million in cash.
Both companies focus on providing integrated telecommunications services to business and residential customers in the upper Midwest. The combined company will be known as McLeodUSA Inc.

Based on the annualized results of the quarter ended March 31, the merged company would have revenues of about $400 million and positive earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $6 million, they added.

"The combined company creates a facilities-oriented telecommunications provider with approximately 200,000 local lines, 4,000 employees, 3,700 route miles of fiber optics network and six switches, focused in a 14-state region, and which also publishes 12 million competitive phone directories a year," Clark McLeod, chairman and chief executive of McLeodUSA, said in a statement.
Dick Lumpkin, chairman and chief executive of Consolidated Communications, added that the two companies are "remarkably complementary."
McLeod said the strategy remains to first build market share, but added it can be accomplished faster through increased sales and marketing strength.
"Our second step is to build network," he addied. "McLeodUSA has over 2,800 route miles of fiber optic network; CCI adds another 900 route miles to that total."

Thirdly, he said McLeodUSA intends to migrate customers to its own network and switches. That strategy is already being executed by Consolidated Communications, with more than 15,000 competitive access lines, three local switching centers and two long distance switching centers, he added.

The companies said they expected to complete the merger within a few months. Consummation of the deal is subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance and approval of the Federal Communications Commission and various state regulatory authorities.
The merger does not require approval by McLeodUSA stockholders because of the number of shares involved in the transaction.

The 8.49 million share of McLeodUSA to be given to Consolidated Communications in the merger represent 13.9 percent of McLeodUSA's outstanding shares. McLeodUSA also will assume Consolidated Communication's debt, which includes long-term debt of about $60 million.
The companies said they expect the merger will be accounted for as a purchase with a substantial portion of the purchase price allocated to intangible assets including goodwill.
